text:
Maya: quick thought — we should standardize the smoke prober contract before the next intake wave, cc @Jamal.
Jamal: yup, the current probes are all over the place. some run full evals, some just token checks. hard to compare cost/latency.
Alex: what are the must-haves for the contract? i'm thinking: 1) deterministic golden inputs 2) kv-cache warmup 3) tokenizer parity check 4) perf microbench + p95/p99
Sasha: + a clear fail/skip policy. e.g. missing ops -> skip with warning; checksum mismatch -> block. otherwise we get noisy flakes. :eyes:
Maya: agreed. proposal: lightweight fast path (smoke) vs heavy path (bench). smoke should be <2s on typical sample and validate compat only (IO shape, tokenizer, kv). bench runs async and collects throughput/latency distributions.
Carol: important callout: some models have dynamic padding behaviors that break our p95 comparisons. smoke should assert correctness not raw latency. latency baselines belong in bench.
Jamal: also need to decide where gating happens: intake (fail fast) or admission (deferred). my take: intake gate enforces interface (+ops present), admission gate enforces perf/quality thresholds.
Alex: that matches our infra. intake is cheap and safe to block on. admission can be queued for dedicated bench infra. We should codify sample sizes: smoke=10 examples, bench=2k tokens aggregated across 100 prompts.
Sasha: sample distributions matter. prefer a stratified set: short, medium, long; streaming vs non-streaming; common tokenization pitfalls (esp. CJK).
Maya: here's a tiny smoke config sketch that could be embedded in the ingest manifest:
```json
{
  "smoke": {
    "samples": 10,
    "timeout_ms": 2000,
    "checks": ["tokenizer_parity", "kv_warmup", "output_shape"]
  },
  "bench": {
    "samples": 2000,
    "metrics": ["p50","p95","p99","throughput"]
  }
}
```
Carol: love that. we also need signal semantics: what constitutes a failure vs regression. e.g. tokenizer_parity fail => block. p95 > baseline * 1.5 => warn + canary. quality regression (>5% on golden set) => block.
Jamal: operationally we should attach ML-team owners for admission failures. smoke failures ping ingest team. add fields to manifest: owner, reclaim_window, fallback_policy.
Alex: fallback_policy could be automatic fallback to quantized/compatible variant (if available) when admission fails but smoke passes. reduces blackout risk.
Sasha: we have to be careful with KV cache verification — running a few next-token steps is enough to detect broken caching, but we should randomize start positions to avoid false positives.
Maya: logging shape for failed smokes: model_id, docker/hash, tokenizer_hash, sample_idx, failing_check, stdout. attach to model registry entry.
smoke-bot: automated run queued: smoke/3500004321 for model "orca-lite-3b". status: queued -> running.
Jamal: one more tradeoff: golden inputs vs synthetic stress. golden gives reproducible quality checks; synthetic finds edge behavior. propose both — smoke uses golden, bench has synthetic stress suite.
Carol: can we-version the probes? when we change smoke checks they should be recorded on the model entry so we can replay old probes.
Alex: yes — manifest should include probe_version and the actual probe bundle checksum.
Sasha: rollout plan? i suggest: 1) add schema + small JS validator in intake 2) enforce smoke checks for all new models for 2 weeks in soft-fail mode (warnings) 3) hard block after we fix top-10 flakes 4) enable admission thresholds for dedicated customers only at first.
Maya: timeline sounds good. I'll draft an RFC with the contract + example manifest + rollout checklist. tagging @Carol and @Alex for review.
Alex: happy to review, will add perf guardrails.
Carol: will add the golden set curation plan.
smoke-bot: smoke/3500004321 finished: 3 failures (tokenizer_parity x2, kv_warmup x1). logs: link <https://internal/storage/3500004321/logs>.
Maya: nice — that's exactly the signal we wanted. i'll open a quick intake ticket to block this model until fixes. :white_check_mark:
